sanskrit_verse:
अतिथित्वेन वर्णानां देयं शक्त्यानुपूर्वशः ।
अप्रणोद्योऽतिथिः सायमपि वाग्भूतृणोदकैः ॥१.१०७॥
transliteration: atithitvena varṇānāṃ deyaṃ śaktyānupūrvaśaḥ | apraṇodyo 'tithiḥ sāyam api vāgbhūtṛṇodakaiḥ || 1.107 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: According to the capacity of each varna, hospitality must be offered to guests in sequential order of ability; a guest is not to be turned away without cause, even in the evening, through speech, offerings, or water.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from svadharma and capacity
Causation arises through conscious duty fulfillment
Restoration occurs when dharma is enacted according to one's śakti
Consciousness alignment manifests through non-rejection of the seeker
executable_legal_axioms: IF entity ∈ varṇa ∧ śakti(entity) ≥ threshold THEN execute_atithi_seva(entity)
IF atithi_arrives(time = any) THEN apraṇodana_check(cause = null) → IF true THEN violation_registered
supreme_court_application: At the highest judicial level, this verse establishes that refusal to serve a guest without just cause constitutes a breach of svadharma. The court must assess not intent but alignment with śakti-based capacity and restoration potential. Legal thresholds are determined by conscious availability, not punitive omission.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa lies in the act of sevā as per śakti. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures proportional fulfillment. Non-punitive reality holds that rejection of atithi disrupts cosmic order; thus, realignment occurs through dharmic completion, not penalty. Cause-effect is traced through conscious engagement, not coercive consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Restore śakti-alignment through guided dharma practice
Reintegrate individual into community through public dharmic reaffirmation
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: Dharma is restored through śakti-anupūrva sevā. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator. All beings align through dharmic action.
